title: Voices and Patches — Lab Journal & Quick Proposals
body:
Purpose and context:
This is a lab-style synthesis of recent customer voices (Jan 2026 — Feb 2026) with small, actionable patches we can iterate on fast. Focus: low-effort fixes that remove friction for Dedicated/Private customers and reduce support noise for Hosted customers. Notes are intentionally informal — treat as a living notebook.

Summary takeaways (quick):
- Three recurring friction families: (1) latency tail / burst handling, (2) billing clarity around reserved vs hosted usage, (3) private onboarding checklist gaps (networking + KMS).
- ~60% of flagged tickets for Dedicated customers are operational (config/scale/fallback) rather than model-quality.
- A set of 6 micro-proposals are likely to reduce CS ticket volume by ~25% for the next quarter if implemented.

Representative customer snippets (verbatim-ish):
- "We see big token spikes after long sessions — instances get stuck in warmup and response times jump to 2s+ for 95th+." — mid-market search SaaS
- "When our reserved hours hit, the billing page still shows hosted usage line items and engineers are unclear what to report to finance." — enterprise fintech
- "Private install guide assumes GCP routes; our on-prem security team needs explicit HSM steps and a diagram." — regulated healthcare

Clustered asks and impact hypothesis:
1) Latency tail (prefix cache + burst handling)
   - Customer problem: sudden long tails at high concurrency after idle periods or long KV growth.
   - Observed signal: support logs show repeated hot-restart of worker VMs, increased cold KV-load misses.
   - Quick patch: expose a "min-warm-concurrency" config on Dedicated pools (default 2). Small change in autoscaler; config in Console. T-shirt: S.
   - Expected impact: reduce 95th latency spikes for small-medium customers; drop 1.2k tickets/yr estimate for Dedicated tier.

2) Billing clarity & token accounting
   - Customer problem: reserved vs hosted lines look duplicated, embedding units and fine-grained metering confusing.
   - Quick patch: add an "explain my bill" CTA on billing page that opens a one-pager with example artifacts (usage sample for last 30 days, how reserved capacity offsets hosted). Also add a CSV export header called "billing_category". T-shirt: XS.
   - Risk: legal/finance review required for wording.

3) Private onboarding — network/KMS checklist gaps
   - Customer problem: missing step for cross-VPC peering and HSM setup leads to 2–3 week delay.
   - Quick patch: create a dedicated Private Onboarding checklist doc with architecture diagram set (include iptables example, KMS policy JSON, sample HSM cert flow). Convert to Console checklist with preflight validator. T-shirt: M.
   - Linked ticket: CS-2418 (see linked_artifacts).

4) Fallback transparency for model variant rollouts
   - Customer problem: customers see sudden model changes (fallback to smaller quantized variant) without clear signal in responses.
   - Quick patch: add subtle response header X-Redwood-Model-Family in streaming and API responses during fallbacks; Console shows last 24h fallback events per route. T-shirt: S.

5) Small UX tweaks to reduce repetitive support flows
   - Problems: repeated requests to reset API keys and trouble understanding route-level quotas.
   - Patches: (a) Add inline tooltip showing "route quota" vs "account quota" on route edit screen; (b) Add a single-click key-rotate that leaves active tokens valid for 15m. T-shirt: XS.

6) Embedded examples + eval prompt sets for regression triage
   - Problem: customers report quality drift after quantization; CS engineers need quick repros.
   - Patch: ship a mini-eval kit per model (10 prompts + expected outputs) visible on model detail pages. T-shirt: M.

Prioritization heuristic used here:
- Effort (XS, S, M) vs direct ticket-reduction vs revenue risk. Prefer XS/S that reduce repeated ops work first.

Unresolved questions / open items (notes to self):
- Do we need a new metric surfaced in Console for "fallback count per 1k requests" or can we reuse existing err/success traces? (cc @Ethan)
- Legal review for billing explanation copy — who owns? Finance or Product? (cc @Lina)
- For Private preflight validator: runbook owner should be SRE or Solutions Eng? Short-term: Solutions Eng builds checklist; SRE signs off.

Implementation notes for eng handoff (concise):
- Autoscaler change for min-warm-concurrency: small delta in policy layer + Console flag. Add e2e test simulating idle period.
- Billing CSV header: backfilling schema for exports; simple UI one-pager stored in Help articles repo.
- Response header: lightweight; add to runtime gateway module and ensure streaming path includes header metadata.

Quick rollout plan (30/60/90):
- 30d: Ship billing CTA & CSV header, route tooltips, one-click rotate.
- 60d: Runtime header for fallback, min-warm-concurrency config behind feature flag (Dedicated only).
- 90d: Private onboarding checklist + preflight validator, mini-eval kit for top 5 models.

Metrics to watch (post-ship):
- CS ticket volume by tag (latency / billing / onboarding). Aim: -25% for latency and billing in 90d.
- Fallback events per route.
- Time-to-first-successful-private-deploy (target: -30% from baseline).

Notes, quick links, and TODOs:
- Draft billing one-pager in confluence and attach to billing CTA: DONE (Lina review pending).
- Prototype of preflight validator: Samuel has a PoC in infra repo; PR around Feb 22.
- Add micro-telemetry for warm-cache rehydration events: TODO @platform-engineering.

Closing thought: focus on short surgical changes that remove triage loops (billing confusion, rate/scale surprise, onboarding checklist). If we can reduce the 3 repetitive triage paths above the CS team can reallocate time to higher-value adoption work (rollouts + performance coaching).

Stamped: Maya Rao — notes in-progress; will convert to in_review when IA on billing text is finalized.
